items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: Did you ever know a person who played with him here in Washington named John W. Dews? No.

ctx.x: I think he was right, yeah.

Did you ever know a person who played with him here in Washington named John W. Dews? No. I encountered this man one night, he was driving a taxi cab, and we got to talk about Jolly Roll, he picked us up over there near where the jungle in was. Oh, yeah. And he said, you know, do you know about Jolly Roll? And I said, well, sure. I said, well, I used to play with him. Is that right? And he played with him apparently a lot. Was it clarinet? He played the reeds, he said.

Well, maybe he was a man, but whoever it was disappointed him. He wrote a tune, and, uh, one night, one night or one afternoon, I tried to get around there when the place wasn't busy, so I wouldn't be interfering with anything. I got around there one afternoon, and he played this thing through, what it was, and I said, well, what's that? He said, a little piece I composed. Composed for a clarinet player, and he was going to meet me down at the United Recording Company down there, and he says he never showed up.…
